decision: Use AI_CHECKS=v2 (coverage judged by exclusions; story check flags only exaggeration).
evidence: Dev set, 48 claims, gpt-5.4-nano, photo prompt v3: v1 32/48 correct, 14 honest held up, 0 wrong approvals; v2 44/48 correct, 2 honest held up, 2 wrong approvals (C012 inflated bill, C022 tyre on rusty car).
pre_registered_rule_result: REJECT (rule: no more wrong approvals). The rule was applied as written and is not changed.
policy_change: The business accepts up to 2 extra wrong approvals on the dev set in exchange for 12 fewer honest customers held up, because every claim is still reviewed by a human adjuster. Both v1-caught cases were caught by accident (photo misreads), not by the check's purpose.
known_limitations: photo severity over-read hides some inflated bills (C012)
old wear read as damage next to a flat tyre makes the tyre exclusion miss (C022)
final_test_plan: Run intake + graph ONCE on the 10 untouched test claims with AI_CHECKS=v2, PHOTO_PROMPT=v3. Report accuracy, wrong approvals and honest claims held up. No changes to prompts or rules after seeing the test result.

decision: AI_ESCALATION=off: the AI writes the note, the rules alone decide the recommendation.
evidence: Dev, 48 claims, nano, checks v2: 44/48 -> 46/48. Fixed C014, C048 (honest claims the AI had escalated). Nothing else changed. Cost $0 (all cached).
rule: honest (written before the run): more honest correct, no fraud scenario worse, tyre not worse, no more wrong approvals.

decision: TYRE_REVIEW=on: if the claimant describes only a tyre but the photo also shows body damage, a human checks (needs_review).
evidence: Dev: wrong approvals 2 -> 1 (C022 now investigate); honest held up 0 -> 2 (C039, C058). As predicted before the run.
rule: money_out (written before the run): fewer wrong approvals, no fraud scenario worse, at most 2 more honest held up.
note: The dev effect was predictable because the dev claims are well known, so the dev run only checked that nothing unexpected broke. The owner chose it as a policy: a wrong payout matters more than a delayed honest claim.
